origins.section: Without volatile, a Reader May Never See the Write: the JIT May Read a Plain Field Once
A Volatile Write Publishes What Was Written Before It, Not What Comes After
volatile Covers One Field: Values That Must Agree Are Swapped as One Immutable Object
volatile Makes Each Read and Each Write Atomic, Never a Read Followed by a Write

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-warmup-loop: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-warmup-loop: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-warmup-loop: The page decides (a): "The JIT compiled the loop, found nothing in it that writes `stop` or synchronizes with another thread, and read the field once, before the loop" and "nothing orders a plain write in one thread before a plain read in another."
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-after-publish: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-after-publish: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-after-publish: The page decides (c): "Its later writes may never reach another thread at all: no volatile write follows them, so nothing publishes them, and a reader may see them, not see them", backed by the demo output "publish, then fill: the dashboard reads rows=0, totalCents=0".
recorded.prompt:q-blocklist: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blocklist: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blocklist: The page decides (c): "Volatile stops at what the field points to. With `volatile Upstream upstream` holding a mutable class, `upstream.port = 6432` is a plain write to a plain field", and the reference table: "a `volatile` reference to a mutable object | a write to one of the object's fields is a plain write".
recorded.prompt:q-heartbeat-long: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heartbeat-long: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heartbeat-long: The page decides (a): "The JLS (§17.7) allows a plain 64-bit write to be done as two 32-bit writes... A reader that falls between the two halves gets a value nobody wrote", with "the risk is on 32-bit JVMs".

recorded.prompt:q-warmup-loop:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-warmup-loop:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-warmup-loop:b: Refuted by "`volatile` takes that freedom away... The JIT must read the field on every iteration" and "It doesn't always do that (a call it can't inline in the loop usually keeps it reading)", so compiled loops do not keep every field in a register for good.
recorded.prompt:q-warmup-loop:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-warmup-loop:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-warmup-loop:c: Refuted directly by "No cache is hiding the write: the hardware keeps caches coherent, and the interpreted loop sees it."
recorded.prompt:q-warmup-loop:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-warmup-loop:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-warmup-loop:d: Refuted by the -Xint run ("plain field: ... still running 1 s later: false"), which shows the interpreted loop sees the write, so no copy was taken at thread start; the page says the compiled loop read the field once before the loop.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-after-publish:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-after-publish:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-after-publish:a: Refuted by the heading "A Volatile Write Publishes What Was Written Before It, Not What Comes After" and the publish-then-fill example, where same-thread writes after the volatile write were not seen.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-after-publish:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-after-publish:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-after-publish:b: Refuted by "Volatile stops at what the field points to... `upstream.port = 6432` is a plain write to a plain field" and by the publish-then-fill demo, where writes through `r` after `latest = r` showed zeros.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-after-publish:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-after-publish:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-after-publish:d: Refuted by "no volatile write follows them, so nothing publishes them" and "may never reach another thread at all", which names the missing volatile write, not a method return, as the reason; the page never gives return any publishing role.
recorded.prompt:q-blocklist:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blocklist:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blocklist:a: Refuted by the rule that a reader that sees the new value sees what "the writer wrote before" its volatile write, together with "the volatile read of `upstream` ... orders nothing" for writes into the object; `add` never writes the field, so there is no volatile write for the read to pair with.
recorded.prompt:q-blocklist:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blocklist:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blocklist:b: Refuted by short inference from "Volatile stops at what the field points to" and "`volatile` makes the read see the latest write and the write visible to the next read, and nothing more": `add` writes inside the object, which are plain writes, not an atomic write of the field.
recorded.prompt:q-blocklist:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blocklist:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blocklist:d: Refuted by "That is how one volatile reference publishes a whole object" and the `volatile Upstream upstream` / `volatile Report latest` examples, which show volatile working on reference fields.
recorded.prompt:q-heartbeat-long:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heartbeat-long:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heartbeat-long:b: Refuted by "a plain 64-bit write to be done as two 32-bit writes": the page describes both halves being written, with the reader falling between them, not the high half being dropped.
recorded.prompt:q-heartbeat-long:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heartbeat-long:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heartbeat-long:c: Refuted directly by the JLS §17.7 sentence and the VarHandle quote that plain accesses are "bitwise atomic only for references and for primitive values of at most 32 bits".
recorded.prompt:q-heartbeat-long:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heartbeat-long:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heartbeat-long:d: Refuted by "A reader that falls between the two halves gets a value nobody wrote", which needs only one writer and one reader; the page sets no two-writer condition.
